A work that redefines the life of Enzo Ferrari, a 20th century giant, one of the most multi-faceted, complex, tormented and imposing figures in Italian history.
The first monumental English edition of this unique book - 984 pages, published by David Bull in 2018 under the title Enzo Ferrari. Power, politics and the making of an automotive empire - has been defined by the New York Times as “the definitive biography of one of the giants of the automotive world”. It was a finalist for the “Motoring Book of the Year Award” promoted by the British Royal Automobile Club that same year, while the previous year the original Italian edition entitled Ferrari Rex published by Giorgio Nada Editore won the 2017 "Selezione Bancarella Sport” Prize.
This new and “reduced” (576 pages), text only version is now being published by Giorgio Nada Editore, rendering accessible to an even broader audience the personal, corporate and sporting aspects of a man who really did write chapters of automotive history on his way to becoming one of the best-known and most charismatic figures of the past century.

About the Author

Luca Dal Monte

Italian author & former automotive executive
Born in Cremona in 1963. His books are read and translated worldwide, spanning biography, investigative non-fiction and fiction — almost always about the people behind sport's greatest stories.
Biography

Two decades in the archives

Over more than two decades, Luca Dal Monte has built a body of work that returns again and again to the same question: what do the choices of ambitious,

...

History and Political Science at the University of Kentucky (1983–1987), Dal Monte returned to Italy to become the Province of Cremona’s first Chief Press Officer. In 1991 he moved into the car industry itself, serving as Chief Press Officer for Peugeot Italy before holding senior communications roles at Toyota Motor Italy, Pirelli, Ferrari and Maserati — the vantage point from which he would eventually turn to writing full-time.
His best-known book, Ferrari Rex , occupied him for the better part of a decade. The idea took shape in the mid-1990s during conversations with motoring journalist Gino Rancati, who had known Enzo Ferrari personally; after Rancati's death, Dal Monte continued the project alone, eventually living in Modena to be close to the people and archives that could tell Ferrari's story from the inside.

In this review

ENZO FERRARI
The definitive biography of an icon 528pp. Cassell. £25.
Luca Dal Monte
Everybody knows Ferrari. Some claim the prancing horse is the most famous brand in the world. This is quite an achievement for a business born from a car dealership in central Italy, and testimony to the vision, perhaps genius, of its founder, Enzo Ferrari. Ferrari implies speed, luxury, elegance, sleekness, but also risk, danger, excitement. How this firm came to be born, and to develop and dominate motor racing for decades, is a fascinating story – one that intersects with Italian history, politics and geography, and with the development of modern capitalism.
This “definitive biography”, translated from the Italian by the author, leaves out much of that history, politics and geography.

...

Luca Dal Monte goes into enormous detail about who won which race, and when, and about the relationships between Ferrari and the drivers he employed, as well as the cars he built, the complicated vicissitudes of his company and his problematic family connections. Its exhaustive dry style feels at times like one list after another. In short, it needed a good edit.
